documents.title: Lump on wrist
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I have a bump on the back of my left wrist that showed up maybe 2 months ago. It doesn't hurt at all. Some days it's bigger and some days I can barely see it. Is this something I should come in for or just watch? I can send a picture if that helps.

documents.title: RE: Lump on wrist
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for writing. Most bumps like that on the back of the wrist are harmless, but I'd like to feel it rather than go by a photo. Can you come in early next week? I'll have the front desk reach out with times.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

orders.reason: Dorsal left wrist swelling, suspected ganglion

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Swelling on the back of the L wrist, first noticed about two months ago. Painless. Size waxes and wanes. No injury she can recall. No numbness, tingling or weakness in the hand. Types all day for work. Otherwise well. No meds. NKDA.

O: Vitals normal. L wrist: roughly 2 cm smooth, mobile swelling over the dorsum of the wrist, nontender, not warm. Overlying skin normal. Full flexion and extension, grip strength 5/5 and symmetric. Sensation intact in median, ulnar and radial distributions. Cap refill brisk. R wrist normal for comparison.

A/P: Dorsal L wrist swelling, exam most suggestive of a ganglion. Discussed that these are benign and often left alone. She would like a hand specialist to look at it since the appearance bothers her and she wants to know her options. Referral to orthopedics & sports medicine placed. Return or message if it becomes painful or she develops numbness.

documents.title: Referral coordination
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Ortho referral sent with last office note. PPO, no auth required per payer line. Orthopedics & sports medicine office scheduled pt for Tue 12/9. Pt notified by text, confirmed.

documents.title: Orthopedics & Sports Medicine Consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
New patient consultation, date of visit 12/09/2025

Re: Hui Huang, DOB 08/11/1997

Dear Doctor,

We saw Ms. Huang at your request for a swelling of the left wrist.

She noticed a soft bump on the dorsum of the left wrist roughly three months ago. It has never hurt. She finds it gets bigger and easier to see when she bends the wrist forward, and it varies in size from week to week. There was no injury. She has had no weakness or numbness in the hand.

Past history: none. Surgeries: none. Medications: none. Allergies: no known drug allergies. Family history: noncontributory. Social: software developer, never smoker, alcohol socially, one or two drinks a month.

Examination of the left wrist: a 2 cm, round, firm, mobile mass sits on the dorsal surface. It transilluminates with a penlight. The skin over it is unremarkable. Wrist motion is full. Motor, sensory and vascular examination of the hand is normal.

Impression: dorsal ganglion cyst, left wrist.

Plan: We reviewed what a ganglion is and that it is benign. Many shrink or settle on their own, so we agreed on a period of observation. She will come back in about three months, or sooner if it becomes painful or she has numbness. Treatment options can be revisited then.

Thank you for allowing us to participate in her care.

Orthopedics & Sports Medicine

documents.title: Ortho visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw the orthopedist Tuesday. They think it's a ganglion like you said and want to just keep an eye on it for now, I go back in March. Did they send you anything?

documents.title: RE: Ortho visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, their letter came in yesterday and I read it. Watching it for a few months is very reasonable. If it starts to hurt or your fingers go numb before March, let me know.

documents.title: Orthopedics & Sports Medicine Follow-up and Procedure
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
Follow-up visit and procedure note, date of visit 03/09/2026

Re: Hui Huang, DOB 08/11/1997

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Huang returned three months after her first visit with us for the left wrist ganglion. Over the six months she has had it, the lump has slowly enlarged. It stands out more after long stretches of typing. Any discomfort is minimal; what bothers her is how it looks. No injury in the interval. Medications: none. Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Exam: on the dorsal left wrist there is a 2 cm, round, rubbery nodule. It moves freely and is not tethered to deeper structures. The skin is intact without redness. It transilluminates. Wrist motion is unrestricted and strength is preserved.

Assessment: dorsal ganglion cyst, left wrist, unchanged in size, cosmetically bothersome.

We talked through continued observation, needle aspiration and surgical excision. She preferred to try aspiration today.

Procedure: aspiration of left dorsal wrist ganglion. Verbal and written consent obtained. Skin prepped sterilely; local anesthetic with lidocaine. Using a large-bore needle, approximately 1 mL of thick, clear, gelatinous fluid was withdrawn. The mass was no longer palpable afterward. Compressive dressing applied. No complications. Fluid not sent.

Plan: keep the dressing on for a couple of days. We explained that ganglia commonly come back after aspiration; if it recurs and still bothers her, excision is the next option. Follow up with us as needed.

Thank you for sending her to us.

Orthopedics & Sports Medicine

documents.title: Wrist update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update - the ortho drained the cyst on my wrist a couple weeks ago. It went fine and it's flat now. Just letting you know, no questions.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
29F here for her annual. Since last year: left dorsal wrist ganglion, seen by ortho in Dec, aspirated in March. Says it has stayed flat since and doesn't bother her at the keyboard. No other interval issues.

Meds none. NKDA. Never smoker, alcohol 1-2 drinks/month.
ROS otherwise negative.
PHQ-9 1.

Exam
VS reviewed, unremarkable; weight about where it has been.
Well-appearing.
HEENT, neck: normal, no thyromegaly.
Heart: regular, no murmur. Lungs: clear.
Abdomen: soft, nontender.
L wrist: no palpable mass over the dorsum, skin normal, full ROM, grip symmetric.
Skin, extremities: normal.

Assessment / plan
1. Health maintenance. CBC/CMP today. Lipids normal 2025, no need to repeat.
2. L wrist ganglion s/p aspiration 03/2026, no recurrence. Taking it off the active problem list. If it comes back, ortho discussed excision.
3. Pap due 2027.
4. Flu shot: nurse visit booked for October. Tdap current.
5. RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Hui, your blood count and metabolic panel are normal. Enjoy the rest of the summer, and we'll see you in October for the flu shot.
